title: Parents of man killed by police feel sorry for officer who pulled the trigger
article: The parents of a man shot dead by police say they'd like to meet the officer who pulled the trigger.
"I'd like to console him a little bit," said dad Carroll Welton, whose son Derek was shot and killed by Mounties in a Duncan trailer park.
"It must be hard for him to have to shoot somebody and I feel very bad for him and I would tell him how sorry I am he had to do this," added Derek's step mom, Ila.
Police were called to a trailer at Duncan R.V. Park & Campground, 2950 Boys Rd., about 6 p.m. Sunday in response to an abandoned 911 call.
When five officers arrived at the trailer, police said they encountered Derek, a 39-year-old with a long history of violence.
A senior officer at the scene who knew Welton engaged the man in a face-to-face conversation in an attempt to calm the situation.
At some point -- police were not clear on this -- Welton armed himself with a knife.
Police said they "utilized multiple force options" including the use of a Taser, without success.
A senior officer with 11 years on the job fired his weapon and hit the male.
Police did not say how many rounds were fired or where Welton was hit, but one unnamed officer said it was a "by the book" shooting.
Police are trained to aim for the chest, or centre of mass, and to "double-tap," or pull the trigger twice.
Paramedics were on scene to give Welton medical assistance before the victim was transported to Cowichan District Hospital, where he later died.
"This is absolutely the worst case scenario for us because when we go to work every day it's to help people," RCMP spokesman Darren Lagan said.
"But it is in the back of each officer's mind that something like this could happen."
The Vancouver Island Integrated Major Crime Unit, an investigational team led by officers of the Victoria Police Dept., is conducting the investigation into the death.
The shooting marks the second homicide at the same trailer park nearly four months to the day of the first.
Bruce Voigt, 67, was charged with second-degree murder for the Nov. 3 shooting death of Robert Harper, a 46-year-old homeless man.
Voigt next appears in Duncan court March 24 to enter a plea to the charges.
When police got the call to go to Derek Welton's trailer, they knew exactly whom they were dealing with, said the dead man's parents.
Carroll and Ila Welton said Derek's problem with alcohol and a dependence on prescription and street drugs meant he could become violent at a moment's notice.
"He'd been Tasered several times," said step mom Ila.
"One time he threw a steak knife at an officer and stuck him in his right leg -- he was cop hater."
Derek, one of four siblings, came to the island soon after his mom died when he was 13.
He lived with the Weltons until he was 18.
Derek made the news several years ago after he crashed his motorcycle near Mount Prevost.
"He smashed his legs bad, really bad and he was lying on railway tracks where no one could have seen him," said Ila.
Odds are Derek would have died where he fell if a German shepherd, dragging its owner, had not found him.
It's then, though, that Derek started doing painkillers, a move that began a lifelong addiction to prescription drugs.
Derek worked for BC hydro for a time before he got sick from using work-related chemicals, said his dad.
Derek had been living on a disability cheque ever since and moved into the trailer park a couple of years ago.
The drugs and alcohol took their toll; Derek had been in and out of jail and various psychiatric wards numerous times.
In fact, Derek had only been out of jail for less than two weeks before he was killed.
"He was violent when he was off drugs and when he was on drugs," Ila said.
Welton's body is expected to undergo an autopsy today in Vancouver and the family said they expect it to be released to them when the post mortem is finished.
A memorial service is planned, but no date had been set by Tuesday.
